heading: Gold's August Surge: What a Weaker Dollar Means for You
tldr: Gold prices witnessed a significant 9% jump in August, driven primarily by external economic factors.
A weaker US Dollar makes gold more affordable for investors holding other currencies, boosting demand.
Expectations of the US Federal Reserve easing its aggressive interest rate hike stance have also contributed to gold's appeal.
This rally pushed spot gold to $4,397 an ounce, though it remains below its January all-time high.
Indian investors holding gold or gold-related assets have seen their portfolio values appreciate this month.
caption:
Ever wonder why gold prices change? Gold went up a lot in August! This is mainly because the US Dollar became a bit weaker. When the Dollar is weaker, gold becomes cheaper for people using other currencies, like the Indian Rupee. This means your gold investments might look better this month.
